Subject: Private CP identity gateway: integration checklist and timeline

Hi Grace / Diane —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, Acme wants to onboard the Redwood Private control plane in their VPC with corporate SSO and group-based access. To keep momentum, here’s a concrete checklist and a couple of clarifying questions so we can run a short integration workshop next week.

High-level asks (we can split these across owners in the workshop):
- Provide SAML IdP metadata URL and sample assertion (including typical group claims).
- Provide SCIM provisioning contact + whether you need push-only "service account" provisioning or bidirectional sync.
- Confirm firewall/egress needs (we assume outbound HTTPS to our private-controlplane.redwood.com metadata endpoints).
- Confirm PKI expectations: we rotate SP certs every 90 days — do you want us to host an ACS metadata endpoint or accept uploaded metadata?

Technical questions for the IdP team:
1) NameID format preference (transient vs persistent) — do you need persistent for session continuity?
2) Group claim name and max groups per assertion (Acme currently uses a mix of nested groups).
3) SCIM token rotation policy and scopes (which operations do you allow: create/update/delete groups/users?).

Our proposed role mapping model (we can iterate):
- redwood-admin -> admins in Acme_Admins group
- redwood-operator -> infra/operator groups
- redwood-viewer -> read-only groups for auditors

Attachments: integration template + network access matrix (see attached). Please drop any docs you already have; Diane, if Okta has a short SCIM checklist we can consume that as input, that’d be great.

Proposed next steps: 30–45m workshop Wednesday (Jun 23) 10:00–10:45 PT — is that OK?

Thanks,

Hi Ben / Grace —

Thanks for the clear checklist. Quick answers from the Okta side and a couple of recommendations based on similar on-prem/private control-plane integrations we’ve seen:

SAML / Assertions:
- We support both transient and persistent NameID; for long-lived sessions we usually recommend persistent with a stable opaque identifier.
- Include these attributes in the assertion: subject (sub), email, groups, displayName. If you want role mapping at SP side include an explicit "roles" claim.
- Max groups per assertion: default limit can be ~150 items; for large orgs we recommend mapping to a group-UID claim instead of embedding all nested groups.

SCIM / Provisioning:
- SCIM v2 push provisioning is supported. Provisioning tokens should be scoped: "Users.write Groups.write" at minimum.
- For service accounts we recommend creating a dedicated SCIM app integration with an application token that rotates monthly.

Metadata & URLs:
- We can expose the IdP metadata URL and generate an SP metadata exchange for you. Please provide your SP ACS URL and entityID.

Network & certs:
- Okta requires that your ACS/metadata endpoints have valid certs trusted by standard CAs. For private endpoints behind a firewall, we recommend using a reverse proxy in the DMZ that terminates TLS and proxies to your SP.

I’m attaching a short Okta SCIM quick-start PDF that covers token scopes and common error cases.

I can join the Wednesday workshop; 10:00 PT works.

Regards,

Thanks Diane — super helpful. A few Redwood-specific notes from the Private Control Plane side (ops and security):

SP/Role mapping model (details):
- SP metadata: our SP entityID for staging will be https://staging-privatecp.redwood.com/saml/metadata and ACS: https://staging-privatecp.redwood.com/saml/acs. Production endpoints are the same hostname under the customer VPC gateway once the tunnel is established.
- We map SCIM groups to our internal roles using a simple mapping table (groupName -> role). We can accept a "roles" claim but prefer SCIM provisioning for authoritative group membership.
- Service accounts: we provision long-lived service accounts for CI or platform automation and assign minimal operator privileges; these are created via SCIM with an attribute "serviceAccount=true" to indicate non-human identities.

Audit & compliance notes:
- All SSO logins funnel into our Control Plane audit log; for Private deployments we additionally ingest SAML assertion metadata into the audit events (IdP entity, assertion id, and Subject) to satisfy audit traces.
- We will require SCIM provisioning events be logged to the customer audit storage endpoint (we support pushing SCIM event webhooks to a customer syslog/HTTPS endpoint).

Action items before workshop:
- Ben: share the integration template + network matrix (done).
- Grace/Acme: provide sample assertion and IdP metadata URL.
- Okta/Diane: confirm SCIM token scope recommendation and share provisioning test user.
- Karthik/Soojin: we'll prepare a draft role-mapping doc and a small staging plan. (I attached the initial draft.)
